title: Newnham College Research Fellowships 2027: Fully Funded Research Opportunities for Outstanding Female Early-Career Researchers Worldwide
summary: Applications are now open for the prestigious Newnham College Research Fellowships 2027 at the University of Cambridge , offering exceptional early-career female researchers from around the world the opportunity to pursue independent research within one of the world s leading academic institutions. Designed to support women at the beginning of their academic careers, these highly competitive fellowships provide generous financial support, research funding, access to an internationally renowned scholarly community, and the freedom to focus exclusively on research for up to three years. The fellowship programme is open to eligible female researchers from any country and spans a broad range of disciplines, including Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Psychology, Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences. If you are an outstanding researcher seeking to advance your academic career at one of the most prestigious universities in the world, this fellowship offers an exceptional platform to develop your research while collaborating with leading scholars across disciplines. About the Newnham College Research Fellowships Newnham College, one of the constituent colleges of the University of Cambridge, has a long-standing commitment to supporting women in higher education and research. Through its Research Fellowship programme, the College provides early-career researchers with the opportunity to establish themselves as independent scholars in a stimulating and supportive academic environment. Research Fellows become part of Newnham College s vibrant scholarly community, where they can engage with academics across diverse disciplines, collaborate with fellow researchers, and participate in the intellectual life of the College. Unlike many academic positions, these fellowships are designed to allow fellows to concentrate primarily on their own research without significant teaching or administrative responsibilities. Research Fellowship Opportunities Available Newnham College currently offers several prestigious research fellowship schemes, including: Junior Research Fellowships (JRF) Early Career Fellowship in Engineering Engineering Research Fellowship Margaret Anstee Research Fellowships Applications are currently invited for selected fellowship schemes, while others will be advertised separately through Newnham College s vacancies page. Junior Research Fellowships The Junior Research Fellowships are intended to support outstanding women researchers during the early stages of their academic careers. These fellowships provide recipients with the time, resources, and academic environment necessary to establish themselves as leading researchers while building strong foundations for future academic appointments. The fellowships are highly competitive and attract applications from exceptional researchers worldwide. Fellowship Duration Successful applicants will normally be appointed for: Three years Although the fellowship runs for three years, some fellows may leave earlier if they secure permanent academic positions at Cambridge or other institutions. Financial Support Successful fellows receive an attractive financial package that includes: A stipend at Point 42 on the University of Cambridge salary scale , valued at £38,784 (2025–26 rate, subject to future pay adjustments) . Annual salary progression over a three-point scale. Potential access to College accommodation available for rent. Research funding to support conference participation and research activities. A one-time allocation of up to £10,000 to organize an approved Newnham-based academic event such as: Conferences Workshops Seminar series These benefits are intended to provide fellows with both financial stability and opportunities to develop their academic networks. Research Environment One of the defining features of the Newnham College Research Fellowships is the opportunity to conduct independent research within one of the world s leading universities. Research Fellows benefit from: A supportive interdisciplinary academic community. Opportunities to collaborate with established researchers. Access to University of Cambridge facilities and resources. Participation in College seminars and academic events. Membership of the College Governing Body. Opportunities to serve on College committees. Although fellows are not required to undertake teaching, they may choose to participate in limited College activities such as: Small-scale teaching. Mentoring postgraduate students. Admissions interviewing. Student pastoral support. Science, Mathematics, Engineering and Psychology Fellowship Applications are currently open for the 2027 Science, Mathematics, Engineering and Psychology Fellowship . Eligible research fields include: Science Mathematics Engineering Psychology Fellowship Start Date 1 October 2027 Application Deadline 3 September 2026 (23:59 local time) Successful applicants may request a deferral of up to three months under exceptional circumstances. Further information and details of how to apply Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences Research Fellowship Newnham College also offers Research Fellowships across Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences through a rotating subject schedule. Subjects Available for the 2027 Fellowship Applications are currently invited in: Classics Geography History and Philosophy of Science Modern and Medieval Languages Theoretical and Applied Linguistics Music Philosophy Fellowship Start Date 1 October 2027 Application Deadline 10 September 2026 (23:59 UK local time) Future Subject Rotations 2028 Eligible disciplines include: Business and Management Divinity Economics English Anglo-Saxon, Norse and Celtic Education History Land Economy Law 2029 Eligible disciplines include: Architecture Asian and Middle Eastern Studies History of Art Human, Social and Political Sciences Archaeology Anthropology Politics and International Studies Social Sciences Further Information and details of how to apply Early Career Fellowship in Engineering Applications are also invited for the 2027 Early Career Fellowship in Engineering . Application Deadline 3 September 2026 (23:59 local time) Fellowship Begins 1 October 2027 Requests to defer the fellowship will only be considered for a maximum of three months. Further information and details of how to apply Newby Trust Research Fellowship Newnham College also administers the prestigious Newby Trust Research Fellowship , offered in partnership with Clare College. Eligible subject areas include: Archaeology Classics Creative and Performing Arts English Language English Literature History Modern Languages Linguistics Music Philosophy Religious Studies Visual Arts and Media This fellowship is offered once every three years by each College in turn. Newnham College will next invite applications in: August 2027 The successful fellow will commence the fellowship on: 1 October 2028 Eligibility Requirements Applicants should note that these fellowships are designed specifically to support women at an early stage of their academic careers. Eligible applicants should: Have recently completed a PhD. Have recently submitted a PhD thesis. Have no more than a few years of full-time postdoctoral research experience. Demonstrate outstanding academic achievement and research potential. Be expected to pursue careers at internationally recognized academic institutions. Importantly: There is no age limit . Applicants who have experienced career breaks for family or professional reasons will not be disadvantaged during the selection process. The fellowships are open to women of all nationalities. Candidates who require a visa to work in the United Kingdom may apply, but appointment is conditional upon obtaining the appropriate visa covering the full duration of the fellowship. Selection Process Given the highly competitive nature of the programme, successful candidates are expected to demonstrate: Academic excellence. Outstanding research achievements. Original and innovative research proposals. Strong future academic potential. Commitment to independent research. For More Information To learn more about the fellowship programmes, eligibility requirements, subject-specific application guidance, and application procedures, applicants should visit the official Newnham College Research Fellowships webpage and consult the relevant application guidance documents for their chosen fellowship. Applicants with questions regarding eligibility may contact: Rebecca Kenny Principal s Executive Assistant Email: rebecca.kenny@newn.cam.ac.uk Applicants are strongly encouraged to review all fellowship guidance documents carefully before submitting their applications. Conclusion The Newnham College Research Fellowships 2027 provide an exceptional opportunity for outstanding early-career female researchers to advance their academic careers within the world-renowned University of Cambridge. With generous financial support, dedicated research time, access to an outstanding scholarly community, and opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration, these fellowships are designed to help promising researchers establish themselves as future leaders in academia. Eligible applicants from around the world are encouraged to prepare their applications early and submit all required documents before the relevant application deadlines in September 2026 . title: ATCMA-ECCAS Call for Expressions of Interest 2026: EU-Funded Opportunity for Timber, Cocoa, and Cassava SMEs in Central Africa
summary: The Programme for Trade Competitiveness and Market Access in Central Africa (ATCMA-ECCAS) has officially launched a Call for Expressions of Interest inviting eligible small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating in the timber, cocoa, and cassava value chains to apply for comprehensive technical support aimed at improving competitiveness, increasing productivity, enhancing product quality, and expanding access to regional, continental, and international markets. Funded by the European Union (EU) and jointly implemented by the International Trade Centre (ITC) and the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) , the programme seeks to strengthen private sector development across Central Africa by helping businesses modernize their operations, adopt sustainable production practices, comply with international quality standards, and unlock new trade and export opportunities. For SMEs seeking to scale their businesses, improve production systems, or enter new markets, this initiative presents a valuable opportunity to receive expert technical assistance without direct financial cost while becoming more competitive in an increasingly global marketplace. About the ATCMA-ECCAS Programme The Programme for Trade Competitiveness and Market Access in Central Africa (ATCMA-ECCAS) is a regional initiative established to improve the competitiveness of businesses throughout the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS). The programme recognizes that many SMEs possess significant production potential but face numerous challenges that limit their ability to compete in both domestic and international markets. These challenges often include outdated production methods, limited value addition, inadequate quality assurance systems, insufficient certification, poor access to export markets, and limited technical capacity. Through targeted technical assistance, the programme aims to help enterprises overcome these barriers while contributing to sustainable economic growth, regional integration, industrial development, and increased trade throughout Central Africa. The initiative is financed by the European Union and implemented through a partnership between two internationally recognized organizations: International Trade Centre (ITC) United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) Together, these organizations provide technical expertise, business development support, and capacity-building services designed to strengthen participating enterprises. Objective of the Call for Expressions of Interest The primary objective of this Call for Expressions of Interest is to identify promising SMEs that are ready to improve their competitiveness and expand their commercial activities. Rather than providing direct financial grants, the programme focuses on delivering specialized technical support that enables businesses to become more efficient, productive, sustainable, and export-ready. Selected companies will receive customized support that addresses their individual business needs while positioning them for long-term growth. Priority Value Chains This call specifically targets enterprises operating within three strategic agricultural and industrial value chains: 1. Timber Eligible timber enterprises may include businesses involved in: Wood processing Timber transformation Furniture manufacturing Timber product value addition Sustainable forestry production Wood exports 2. Cocoa The programme welcomes cocoa enterprises involved in: Cocoa production Cocoa processing Chocolate manufacturing Cocoa value addition Packaging Export development 3. Cassava Cassava businesses operating in areas such as: Cassava processing Food manufacturing Industrial cassava products Value-added cassava products Commercial production Export-oriented activities are encouraged to apply. Programme Areas of Support The ATCMA-ECCAS programme focuses on strengthening businesses across several important areas. 1. Local Processing and Product Upgrading Participating enterprises will receive support to: Improve processing techniques. Increase product value. Diversify product offerings. Produce higher-quality finished products. Reduce post-harvest losses. Improved local processing helps businesses capture more value before products enter domestic or export markets. 2. Strengthening Productive and Commercial Capacity The programme helps SMEs become stronger businesses by supporting: Improved production efficiency. Better operational management. Increased productivity. Business planning. Market positioning. Commercial growth. 3. Improving Quality Standards and Certification Meeting international standards is essential for accessing high-value export markets. The programme supports businesses through: Quality management improvements. Compliance with international standards. Certification support. Product traceability. Food safety systems where applicable. Sustainable production standards. 4. Regional and International Market Integration Selected enterprises will receive guidance to access: National markets. Regional markets. Continental markets. International export opportunities. The programme encourages businesses to become competitive suppliers capable of meeting international buyer requirements. 5. Sustainable Business Practices Modern markets increasingly demand sustainability. The programme promotes: Environmentally responsible production. Sustainable sourcing. Resource efficiency. Responsible manufacturing. Competitive green business practices. 6. Trade and Export Development Businesses will also receive assistance to: Expand exports. Identify buyers. Improve market access. Participate in trade promotion activities. Strengthen commercial relationships. Technical Support Available Selected companies will benefit from a comprehensive package of technical assistance tailored to their business needs. Support may include the following. Company Diagnostics Experts will conduct detailed assessments of participating enterprises to identify strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and priority improvement areas. Development of Upgrading Plans Each company may receive a customized upgrading roadmap outlining practical actions needed to improve competitiveness and business performance. Modernization Support The programme assists enterprises in modernizing operations through: Improved production methods. Technology adoption. Operational improvements. Increased efficiency. Digitalisation Support Businesses will receive assistance in integrating digital tools that enhance productivity, management, marketing, and commercial operations. Production Process Improvement Experts will help companies optimize production systems to improve quality, efficiency, and consistency. Technical Training Participants will benefit from specialized training covering: Production techniques. Business management. Export readiness. Product quality. Sustainable practices. Coaching and Mentorship Businesses will receive personalized coaching from experienced experts who will provide guidance throughout the improvement process. Quality and Certification Support Technical experts will help companies: Improve product quality. Prepare for certification. Strengthen traceability systems. Meet export compliance requirements. Sustainable Production Practices The programme encourages adoption of sustainable production methods that improve competitiveness while protecting environmental resources. Commercial Development Businesses will receive support in: Business expansion. Market development. Sales improvement. Customer acquisition. Export Development Participating enterprises will be assisted in preparing for international trade through export readiness support. Trade Fairs and Business Meetings Selected companies may receive support to participate in: Trade fairs. International exhibitions. Business matchmaking events. Commercial networking opportunities. These activities provide valuable exposure to potential buyers, investors, and commercial partners. Eligibility Requirements To qualify for this Call for Expressions of Interest, applicants must satisfy all four of the following conditions. 1. Legal Registration The business must be legally registered within an ECCAS Member State. 2. Operate in Eligible Value Chains The company must operate within one of the following sectors: Timber Cocoa Cassava 3. Active Business Operations Only companies that are currently operational and actively conducting business are eligible. 4. Commitment to Growth Applicants should demonstrate a clear intention to: Improve competitiveness. Expand commercial activities. Strengthen production capacity. Develop export opportunities. The programme will verify compliance with these requirements using information provided in the application questionnaire and supporting documentation. Application Process Interested companies must complete the official Expression of Interest questionnaire. Estimated Completion Time Approximately 15 minutes . Applicants should ensure that all submitted information is accurate, complete, and supported by the required documentation. Data Confidentiality All information submitted through the application process will be handled confidentially. The collected information will be used exclusively for: Selecting beneficiary companies. Implementing programme activities. Monitoring programme implementation. Programme evaluation. By submitting an application, each company confirms that: The information provided is accurate. The information is complete. It agrees to data processing for programme implementation. It will actively participate in programme activities if selected. It will cooperate with programme experts during diagnostics and implementation. Contact Information Applicants with questions regarding this Call for Expressions of Interest may contact the programme team through the following email addresses: DWANDJI@intracen.org S.MEVONOANGON@unido.org hbangda@intracen.org Important Deadline Application Deadline: 21 August 2026 Applicants are encouraged to complete and submit their applications well before the closing date to avoid last-minute technical issues or incomplete submissions. APPLY HERE Why Businesses Should Apply Participation in the ATCMA-ECCAS programme offers SMEs a unique opportunity to receive expert technical assistance that can transform their operations and improve their long-term competitiveness. Key advantages include: Access to international technical expertise. Business diagnostics and tailored upgrading plans. Improved production systems. Enhanced product quality. Support for certification and compliance. Export readiness assistance. Commercial development support. Participation in trade fairs and business events. Increased competitiveness in regional and global markets. Adoption of sustainable and modern business practices. Rather than providing one-time financial assistance, the programme focuses on building lasting business capacity that enables enterprises to grow sustainably over the long term. Visit HERE for more information about the ATCMA-ECCAS Call for Expressions of Interest 2026. Conclusion The ATCMA-ECCAS Call for Expressions of Interest is an outstanding opportunity for SMEs operating in the timber, cocoa, and cassava value chains across Central Africa to strengthen their businesses and expand into new markets. Through the combined expertise of the European Union, the International Trade Centre, and the United Nations Industrial Development Organization, selected enterprises will receive tailored technical support aimed at improving productivity, quality, sustainability, and export readiness. Businesses that meet the eligibility requirements should take advantage of this opportunity by submitting their applications before the 21 August 2026 deadline and positioning themselves for sustainable commercial growth in regional and international markets. title: Free UN Sustainable Finance Courses with Digital Certificates: Learn Sustainable Finance, Green Finance, SDG Financing, and Sustainable Finance Taxonomies
summary: As the world accelerates efforts to combat climate change and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), sustainable finance has become one of the most important areas of knowledge for policymakers, financial professionals, businesses, researchers, students, and development practitioners. Financial institutions and governments across the globe are increasingly integrating sustainability into investment decisions, banking, insurance, lending, and economic policies. To help build global capacity in this rapidly growing field, UN CC:Learn offers a collection of self-paced online courses that provide participants with practical and technical knowledge on sustainable finance. These courses are designed by leading international organizations and financial institutions and provide learners with the opportunity to earn an official UN digital certificate upon successful completion. Among the most valuable learning opportunities currently available are: Introduction to Sustainable Finance Introduction to Sustainable Finance Taxonomies SDG Learncast Microlearning: Global Finance in Transition – Reforming the Global Financial System for the SDGs These learning opportunities are suitable for professionals seeking to strengthen their understanding of sustainable development financing, green finance instruments, climate finance, financial regulations, and the transformation of global financial systems. Why Sustainable Finance Matters Sustainable finance refers to financial activities that integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations into investment and financial decision-making. Rather than focusing solely on short-term financial returns, sustainable finance promotes investments that contribute to: Climate change mitigation Climate adaptation Environmental protection Social inclusion Responsible governance Long-term economic growth Achievement of the UN Sustainable Development Goals Implementation of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change Governments, banks, investment firms, insurance companies, regulators, development organizations, and businesses are increasingly adopting sustainable finance principles to ensure that financial resources contribute to a more resilient and inclusive global economy. The UN CC:Learn courses provide participants with foundational and practical knowledge needed to understand this evolving field. Course 1: Introduction to Sustainable Finance Course Overview The Introduction to Sustainable Finance course is an interactive, self-paced online programme that provides comprehensive technical knowledge about the contribution of sustainable finance to sustainable development. Originally developed in 2018 and extensively updated in 2021, the course combines theory with practical examples, enabling participants to understand how sustainability considerations can be integrated into financial systems and policy frameworks. Course Information Learning mode: Self-paced Duration: Approximately 10 hours Language: English Certificate available Digital certification fee: USD 20 Platform: UN CC:Learn Learning Objectives Participants will gain the ability to: Understand how sustainable finance supports the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Explain how sustainable finance contributes to implementing the Paris Climate Agreement. Understand the core principles of sustainable finance. Identify sustainability risks and opportunities within financial systems. Learn how governments and regulators shape sustainable finance. Explore major sustainable finance products. Understand sustainable finance regulations and industry initiatives. Learn how financial institutions integrate sustainability into investment decisions. Course Modules The programme consists of four comprehensive modules. Module 1: Sustainable Finance in Context This introductory module explores: Global climate challenges Sustainable development priorities The relationship between finance and sustainable development The role of finance in achieving international environmental goals Module 2: Fundamentals of Sustainable Finance This module introduces the basic concepts of sustainable finance, including: ESG considerations Financial decision-making Sustainable investment approaches Sustainability risk management Financial sector responsibilities Module 3: Sustainable Finance Regulation and Self-Regulation Participants explore: Government regulations Financial sector standards Industry initiatives Voluntary sustainability frameworks Regulatory developments around the world Module 4: Sustainable Finance Products Learners discover major financial products that support sustainable development, including: Green bonds Sustainability bonds Social bonds Green loans Sustainability-linked loans Climate finance instruments UN Digital Certificate Participants who score at least 70% on all quizzes become eligible for a UN Digital Certificate. Important requirements include: Minimum passing score: 70% Maximum of three attempts per quiz Certificate issued after payment of USD 20 Certificate can be downloaded and shared digitally The digital certificate provides internationally recognized evidence of successful completion. Course Partners The course was developed through collaboration between internationally recognized organizations including: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken (SEB) Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) These organizations collectively contribute extensive expertise in sustainable finance, green bond markets, climate finance, and international development. APPLY HERE Visit HERE to learn more about the Introduction to Sustainable Finance. Course 2: Introduction to Sustainable Finance Taxonomies Course Overview The Introduction to Sustainable Finance Taxonomies course focuses on one of the fastest-growing areas of sustainable finance: sustainable finance taxonomies. Taxonomies help governments, investors, regulators, and businesses classify economic activities according to sustainability criteria, making it easier to direct investments toward environmentally and socially responsible activities. The course combines practical case studies with technical guidance to help participants understand how taxonomies are designed and implemented. Course Details Duration: 3.5–4 hours Learning mode: Self-paced Price: Free Certificate fee: USD 15 Languages: English Spanish French Platform: UN CC:Learn Learning Objectives Participants will learn: What sustainable finance taxonomies are Why taxonomies are important How taxonomies mobilize sustainable investment Principles used when developing taxonomies International best practices National implementation strategies Real-world applications Course Modules Module 1: Overview of Sustainable Finance Taxonomies Covers: Definition of taxonomies Purpose Key concepts Importance for sustainable finance Module 2: Taxonomies in Practice Examines practical examples from: European Union China Participants understand how different jurisdictions classify sustainable economic activities. Module 3: Principles of Taxonomy Development This module explains: Design principles Governance Technical screening criteria Transparency Interoperability Module 4: Taxonomy Development in Practice Uses detailed case studies from: South Africa Colombia These examples demonstrate how countries adapt international best practices to local priorities. UN Digital Certificate Participants who successfully pass the final assessment with at least 70% become eligible for a UN Digital Certificate. Certificate details include: Passing score: 70% Maximum of three quiz attempts Certificate fee: USD 15 Organizations Behind the Course The course was developed through collaboration among: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) Sustainable Banking and Finance Network (SBFN) International Finance Corporation (IFC) World Bank Group These institutions contribute global expertise in sustainable banking, financial sector reforms, and climate finance. APPLY HERE Visit HERE to learn more about the Introduction to Sustainable Finance Taxonomies. Bonus Learning Resource: Global Finance in Transition – Reforming the Global Financial System for the SDGs In addition to the structured courses, learners can also access the SDG Learncast podcast episode titled: Global Finance in Transition: Reforming the Global Financial System for the SDGs The episode features Guillaume Lafortune, Vice President of the Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN), discussing major challenges affecting financing for sustainable development. Topics Covered The discussion explores: Why progress toward the SDGs has slowed The estimated global SDG financing gap Long-term financing strategies Climate finance Reforming global financial architecture Role of multilateral development banks Financing infrastructure Human capital investments Renewable energy investments Water investments Public and private financing Global taxation mechanisms Domestic resource mobilization Credit rating reforms Governance reforms International cooperation The podcast emphasizes that achieving the SDGs requires significant reforms to global financial systems and increased investment in sustainable development, particularly in developing countries. Benefits of Enrolling Participants who complete these learning opportunities will benefit from: High-quality UN-developed learning materials Flexible self-paced learning Practical case studies International perspectives Technical knowledge on sustainable finance Better understanding of ESG principles Knowledge of sustainable finance regulations Exposure to green finance products Skills relevant to banking, government, development organizations, and the private sector Official UN Digital Certificate (upon meeting requirements and paying the applicable certification fee) Who Should Enroll? These courses are ideal for: Government officials Policymakers Financial regulators Central bank staff Banking professionals Investment professionals Financial analysts Researchers University students Academics Climate professionals Sustainability consultants Development practitioners Civil society organizations Private sector professionals Corporate sustainability teams NGOs International development professionals The Sustainable Finance Taxonomies course is particularly relevant for policymakers, regulatory authorities, ministries, central banks, capital market authorities, and organizations preparing for taxonomy reporting requirements. Certification Requirements To receive the official UN Digital Certificate: Introduction to Sustainable Finance Complete all modules Pass every quiz with at least 70% Maximum three attempts per quiz Pay USD 20 certificate fee Introduction to Sustainable Finance Taxonomies Complete all modules Score at least 70% on the final quiz Maximum three attempts Pay USD 15 certificate fee Is There an Application Deadline? There is currently no application deadline. Since both courses are self-paced and continuously available through the UN CC:Learn platform, learners can enroll at any time and study according to their own schedule. APPLY HERE Visit HERE to learn more about the Global Finance in Transition Why These Courses Stand Out Unlike many introductory online courses, these programmes combine policy, finance, sustainability, and international development into one comprehensive learning experience. They are developed with contributions from globally recognized organizations, including UN agencies, development banks, financial institutions, and government partners. Whether you are pursuing a career in sustainable finance, preparing for work in climate policy, supporting green investment initiatives, or simply expanding your understanding of the global transition toward sustainable development, these courses provide valuable knowledge grounded in international best practices. Conclusion The transition to a sustainable global economy depends heavily on the financial sector s ability to mobilize investments that generate environmental, social, and economic benefits. The UN CC:Learn sustainable finance courses provide learners with accessible, high-quality education on the principles, tools, regulations, and financial products driving this transformation. Through interactive lessons, practical case studies, and expert insights, participants gain a strong foundation in sustainable finance and sustainable finance taxonomies while exploring the broader reforms needed to close the global financing gap for the Sustainable Development Goals. With flexible self-paced learning, internationally recognized digital certificates, and no enrollment deadline, these courses offer an excellent opportunity for professionals, students, policymakers, and organizations worldwide to build essential knowledge and contribute to a more sustainable future. title: MMoCRA Scholarships 2026: Apply for EU-Funded Master’s and PhD Academic Mobility Opportunities for Climate-Resilient Research Across Africa
summary: Applications are officially open for the Multidisciplinary Mobility for a Climate Resilient Africa (MMoCRA) Scholarships 2026 , an academic mobility initiative funded by the European Union through the Intra-Africa Academic Mobility Scheme . The MMoCRA programme connects leading African and European universities to strengthen climate resilience across Africa through multidisciplinary education, research, training, academic mobility, and knowledge exchange. Through the programme, students, researchers, trainees, and university staff can participate in mobility opportunities intended to strengthen the continent s scientific and technical capacity to address climate change and sustainable development challenges. For the current application round, MMoCRA is accepting applications for Master’s and PhD scholarships , providing successful applicants with opportunities to pursue academic mobility at participating African universities while contributing to research and innovation addressing some of Africa s most pressing challenges. The programme covers multidisciplinary areas including Climate and Energy, Digital Technologies, Critical Raw Materials, Agrifood Systems, and broader multidisciplinary climate solutions . Applications opened on 31 July 2026 , and interested candidates must submit their applications by 15 September 2026 at 5:00 PM East Africa Time (EAT) . About the Multidisciplinary Mobility for a Climate Resilient Africa Programme The Multidisciplinary Mobility for a Climate Resilient Africa , commonly referred to as MMoCRA , is an EU-funded academic mobility programme operating through the Intra-Africa Academic Mobility Scheme. Its overarching purpose is to strengthen climate resilience across Africa by connecting universities and facilitating multidisciplinary research, training, academic mobility, and knowledge exchange. Climate change presents complex challenges that cannot be adequately addressed by a single academic discipline. Building climate-resilient societies requires expertise across areas such as energy, agriculture, engineering, digital technologies, natural resources, food systems, environmental science, and other related disciplines. MMoCRA responds to this need by supporting multidisciplinary academic cooperation and helping develop a new generation of African scientists, researchers, engineers, and professionals capable of designing and implementing innovative climate-resilient solutions. Through academic mobility and collaboration between participating institutions, the programme seeks to contribute to sustainable development while strengthening the research and human capacity of African universities. MMoCRA Scholarships 2026: Applications Now Open The MMoCRA Project has officially announced that applications are open for its Master’s and PhD scholarships under the Intra-Africa Academic Mobility Scheme . This opportunity is intended for candidates who are ready to take their academic journey beyond national borders and participate in research addressing major development challenges facing Africa. Successful applicants will have an opportunity to study at leading participating African universities while contributing to research, innovation, and knowledge creation relevant to climate resilience and sustainable development. Key Application Dates Applications Open: 31 July 2026 Application Deadline: 15 September 2026 at 5:00 PM EAT Applicants should ensure that their complete applications are submitted before the stated deadline. What Is the Intra-Africa Academic Mobility Scheme? MMoCRA operates within the framework of the Intra-Africa Academic Mobility Scheme and is funded by the European Union. Within MMoCRA, academic mobility is used as a mechanism to connect universities, researchers, students, trainees, and staff while encouraging the exchange of knowledge and expertise. The programme s emphasis on mobility means participants can gain academic and research experience beyond their existing institutional environments while strengthening collaboration between participating universities. Through this approach, MMoCRA seeks to build stronger academic connections and develop expertise capable of responding to climate and sustainable development challenges across Africa. 95 Mobility Scholarships and Opportunities Under MMoCRA The overall MMoCRA programme indicates a total of 95 mobility scholarships/opportunities across several categories. These comprise: 44 Master’s opportunities 12 Doctoral opportunities 20 Trainee opportunities 19 Staff opportunities Together, these amount to 95 mobility opportunities . This demonstrates that MMoCRA is designed as a broader academic mobility and capacity-building programme involving different levels of the university and research ecosystem. It is important, however, to distinguish the overall programme structure from the current call described in the supplied announcement. The current announcement specifically states that applications are open for Master’s and PhD scholarships . Although the MMoCRA website also identifies trainee and staff mobility within the overall programme, the information supplied does not state that trainee and staff applications are included in this particular application round. Click HERE to learn more MMoCRA Master’s Scholarships MMoCRA identifies 44 Master’s mobility opportunities within its overall mobility programme. These opportunities form the largest component of the 95 mobility places identified by the programme. The Master’s mobility component provides postgraduate students with opportunities to undertake academic study and engage with research relevant to Africa s climate resilience and sustainable development needs. Successful applicants can benefit from exposure to participating universities, multidisciplinary learning environments, and research addressing practical African challenges. MMoCRA Doctoral Scholarships The programme also includes 12 doctoral mobility opportunities . PhD-level mobility is particularly important to MMoCRA s objective of developing advanced research expertise capable of generating innovative solutions for climate resilience. Doctoral participants can contribute to the development of knowledge in fields relevant to the programme while strengthening research collaboration between participating universities. The current application announcement explicitly confirms that applications are being accepted for PhD scholarships . Trainee Mobility Opportunities The overall MMoCRA structure identifies: 20 trainee mobility opportunities. These form another component of the programme s broader academic and professional capacity-building strategy. However, the supplied application announcement specifically calls for applications for Master s and PhD scholarships. It does not provide application instructions, eligibility requirements, or a separate deadline for trainee mobility. Prospective trainees should therefore consult the official MMoCRA platform for calls specifically applicable to this category. Staff Mobility Opportunities MMoCRA also identifies: 19 staff mobility opportunities. Staff mobility can support institutional knowledge exchange and strengthen connections among participating universities. Again, the current announcement supplied for this article specifically concerns applications for Master s and PhD scholarships and does not provide detailed application instructions for the staff category. Academic and Research Focus Areas One of the defining characteristics of MMoCRA is its multidisciplinary approach. The programme website identifies broad focus areas including: Climate and Energy Agrifood Systems Multidisciplinary Climate Solutions The current scholarship announcement further highlights: Climate and Energy Digital Technologies Critical Raw Materials Agrifood, Climate and Energy Together, these areas reflect the programme s emphasis on combining different academic and technical disciplines to strengthen climate resilience and sustainable development. 1. Climate and Energy Climate and energy are central to MMoCRA s mission. Africa s sustainable development is closely connected to its capacity to respond to changing climatic conditions while developing resilient and sustainable energy systems. Research and academic training within this area can contribute to building expertise relevant to climate resilience, energy systems, environmental sustainability, and related challenges. MMoCRA provides a platform through which students and researchers can contribute academic knowledge to these broader continental priorities. 2. Digital Technologies The scholarship announcement specifically identifies Digital Technologies as one of the focus areas. Digital technologies are increasingly relevant to research, innovation, data-driven decision-making, and the development of solutions to complex environmental and development challenges. The inclusion of digital technologies reinforces the multidisciplinary nature of MMoCRA and provides opportunities for research that connects technological innovation with climate resilience and sustainable development. 3. Critical Raw Materials Critical Raw Materials are also identified among the focus areas in the current scholarship announcement. The inclusion of this field reflects the broader relationship between natural resources, technology, energy systems, economic development, and sustainability. Students whose academic and research interests connect with critical raw materials and the programme s wider climate-resilience objectives may therefore find MMoCRA particularly relevant. 4. Agrifood Systems MMoCRA identifies Agrifood Systems as another major focus area. Climate change has significant implications for agricultural production and food systems, making climate-resilient agrifood systems an important area of research and innovation. Through multidisciplinary research and academic mobility, the programme seeks to strengthen expertise capable of contributing to sustainable and resilient solutions. 5. Agrifood, Climate and Energy The current call also highlights the interconnected area of Agrifood, Climate and Energy . Rather than approaching these issues independently, MMoCRA s multidisciplinary framework recognizes the relationships between food production, environmental conditions, energy systems, and sustainable development. This integrated approach can enable researchers to examine complex challenges through multiple academic perspectives. 6. Multidisciplinary Climate Solutions Beyond individual fields, MMoCRA places particular emphasis on multidisciplinary climate solutions . Climate resilience involves interconnected environmental, technological, agricultural, economic, and social challenges. The programme therefore seeks to encourage research and training capable of crossing traditional disciplinary boundaries and producing innovative approaches relevant to sustainable development in Africa. title: Fund for SIDS Partnerships – United Nations Awards 2026 Recognizing Sustainable Development Excellence
summary: Introduction Fund for SIDS Partnerships is a cornerstone initiative of the United Nations, designed to recognize and reward the most genuine, durable, and impactful collaborations that advance the sustainable development priorities of Small Island Developing States (SIDS). These nations, spread across the Caribbean, Pacific, Atlantic, and Indian Oceans, face unique vulnerabilities: climate change, rising sea levels, economic fragility, limited resources, and geographic isolation. Yet, they also embody resilience, innovation, and community‑driven solutions that inspire global action. The SIDS Partnerships Awards , established in 2021, emerged from a decade of international dialogue on how partnerships can drive sustainable development. The awards are rooted in the SAMOA Pathway and strengthened by the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS (ABAS) , adopted at the Fourth International Conference on SIDS (SIDS4) in 2024. They highlight partnerships that embody principles of mutual collaboration, trust, alignment, accountability, transparency, and innovation. The 2026 Awards are particularly significant. They arrive at a time when SIDS are advancing ABAS implementation, strengthening the SIDS Partnership Framework, and preparing for the High‑Level Political Forum (HLPF). The awards showcase partnerships that translate commitments into concrete results, demonstrate solidarity with SIDS, and reinforce the collaboration needed to support their sustainable development. By recognizing partnerships across the three dimensions of sustainable development—economic, social, and environmental—the awards amplify the voices of SIDS, motivate new collaborations, and incentivize the registration of partnerships under the UN framework. They are not simply accolades; they are catalysts for action, visibility, and replication of best practices worldwide. Why Apply? The SIDS Partnerships Awards provide opportunities to: Showcase partnerships as global good practices. Gain recognition through the United Nations. title: Investigative Journalism Grant – IWMF Fault Lines Fund for U.S. Hate Narrative Reporting
summary: Introduction The IWMF Fault Lines Reporting Fund supporting investigative journalism has become essential in today’s polarized media environment. Hate‑based narratives in the United States—ranging from racism, antisemitism, Islamophobia, and misogyny—are no longer confined to fringe spaces. They have infiltrated mainstream discourse, fueled by misinformation and disinformation campaigns, and are actively shaping public opinion while endangering marginalized communities. The International Women’s Media Foundation (IWMF) created the Fault Lines Reporting Fund to address this urgent need. This three‑year program provides grants to staff and freelance journalists committed to uncovering the forces driving intolerance and exposing harmful narratives that normalize hate. By resourcing investigative, evidence‑based reporting, the fund empowers journalists to challenge misinformation, hold power accountable, and amplify the voices of communities resisting hate. The rise of hate‑based narratives in the United States represents one of the most urgent challenges facing journalism today. What once existed in fringe spaces—dark online channels, extremist forums, and special interest groups—has increasingly seeped into mainstream discourse. Racism, antisemitism, Islamophobia, misogyny, and other forms of intolerance are no longer confined to the margins; they are amplified by misinformation and disinformation campaigns, shaping public opinion and fueling violence against marginalized communities. Journalists are uniquely positioned to confront these narratives, but investigative reporting requires resources, time, and support. Recognizing this need, the International Women’s Media Foundation (IWMF) established the Fault Lines Reporting Fund . This three‑year program provides grants to staff and freelance journalists committed to uncovering the forces driving intolerance and exposing the harmful narratives that normalize hate. The fund is designed to support well‑researched, evidence‑based reporting projects that go beyond surface coverage. Successful applications will examine how divisive stories take hold, what fuels them, where they are most pronounced, and the scope of their impact. By resourcing journalists to pursue these critical investigations, the IWMF aims to strengthen press freedom, elevate women journalists, and transform the global news media. This initiative is not just about funding—it is about empowering journalists to challenge misinformation, hold power to account, and amplify the voices of communities resisting hate. It is about ensuring that journalism continues to serve as a cornerstone of democracy, truth, and equity. Duration: Three years. Funding: Grants for staff and freelance journalists. Focus: Stories that uncover how hate‑based narratives spread and their impact on communities. Reporting Focus Areas Journalists supported by the Fault Lines Reporting Fund are encouraged to explore: Origins of hate‑based narratives – tracing how they emerge from fringe media, dark channels, or special interest groups. Mainstream adoption – analyzing how these narratives gain traction in prominent outlets or political discourse. Impact on communities – documenting the violence, discrimination, and fear these narratives fuel. Mechanisms of spread – investigating the role of social media, misinformation networks, and organized campaigns. Resistance and resilience – highlighting communities and individuals countering hate with truth, solidarity, and advocacy. A three‑year grant program by the IWMF supporting journalists investigating hate‑based narratives in the U.S. Who funds the program? Staff and freelance journalists planning investigative reporting projects in the United States. What types of stories are supported? By providing financial support and institutional backing, the IWMF ensures that journalists—whether staff reporters or freelancers—can pursue ambitious, evidence‑based investigations without compromise. title: Disaster Risk Reduction Training – UNITAR Women’s Leadership Programme for World Tsunami Awareness Day 2026
summary: Introduction Disasters do not discriminate—but their impacts often do. From tsunamis and cyclones to floods and earthquakes, the consequences of these events ripple through societies, often exacerbating existing inequalities. Women, in particular, are frequently at the forefront of caregiving, community rebuilding, and resource management, yet their leadership in disaster risk reduction (DRR) has historically been underrecognized and underfunded. Recognizing this gap, the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) has launched a transformative initiative: the Women’s Leadership in Disaster Risk Reduction Training Programme for World Tsunami Awareness Day 2026 , generously funded by the Government and People of Japan. This programme is not just about training—it is about reshaping the narrative of disaster preparedness by centering women’s voices, experiences, and leadership. The initiative aims to equip 500 participants with lifelong skills in disaster risk reduction and inclusive leadership. It is designed to strengthen resilience, empower women, and promote equitable participation in disaster preparedness and response. By drawing from Japan’s globally respected disaster management expertise and contextualizing lessons within the Asia‑Pacific region, the programme ensures that participants gain both technical knowledge and culturally relevant strategies. This training is more than an educational opportunity—it is a call to action. It invites motivated individuals to step forward, learn, and lead their communities toward resilience. title: OpenAI Student Collective 2026–2027: Apply to Become a Campus Lead and Receive Funding, ChatGPT Access, Codex Credits and a Cash Stipend
summary: Applications are now open for the OpenAI Student Collective 2026–2027 , a campus leadership initiative designed to empower undergraduate students to help their peers learn, experiment with, and confidently use artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT and Codex. Through the Student Collective, selected undergraduate students will serve as OpenAI Campus Leads , working in pairs to create active AI learning communities at their colleges and universities. Campus Leads will organize workshops, facilitate weekly project-building sessions, host campus showcases, and help students from different academic disciplines discover practical and creative ways to use AI. The opportunity comes with substantial support from OpenAI. Campus Leads will receive a ChatGPT subscription, Codex credits, funding and resources for campus events, merchandise, training, guidance from OpenAI, access to a global network of Campus Leads, and a cash stipend each semester in recognition of their time and leadership. There may also be opportunities for selected participants to visit OpenAI headquarters in June 2027 . The program is initially available to eligible undergraduate students studying in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, France, Germany, India, Japan, and South Korea . Students studying elsewhere can still submit an application to register their interest for possible future availability. Applications close on August 10, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time (PT). About the OpenAI Student Collective Students have been among the early adopters finding new ways to use artificial intelligence for learning, creativity, problem-solving, project development, and other academic and everyday activities. As AI tools become increasingly capable, students are likely to play an important role in determining how these technologies are understood and applied within universities. The OpenAI Student Collective seeks to support that student-led experimentation by establishing communities where learners can develop practical AI skills together. Rather than limiting participation to computer science, engineering, or technology students, OpenAI encourages students from every academic discipline to participate. The central leadership role within the program is the Campus Lead . Campus Leads will help create an environment on their campuses where students can: Learn about the latest AI tools. Develop confidence using ChatGPT and Codex. Experiment with practical AI applications. Begin and develop their own projects. Work alongside students from other academic disciplines. Receive help when they encounter challenges. Showcase projects they have created. Participate in a broader student AI community. OpenAI is particularly looking for undergraduate students who are curious, community-minded, interested in its tools, and enthusiastic about helping other students learn. How the OpenAI Student Collective Works Campus Leads will work in pairs to build and maintain their campus communities. The Student Collective is structured around four major components: Workshops, Studio Hours, Showcases, and Community. 1. Workshops Campus Leads will organize welcoming workshops where students can develop new AI skills and explore what they can create using available tools. These workshops are intended to help participants move from learning about AI to actually using it. Students can then choose projects or ideas that they want to continue developing during subsequent Studio Hours. Campus Leads are expected to organize: Four workshops per semester. These activities will therefore form an important part of the Student Collective s learning experience. 2. Weekly Studio Hours Studio Hours provide regular opportunities for students to work on their projects in a collaborative environment. They will be held: Weekly. Instead of learning something during a workshop and then working completely independently, participants can return to Studio Hours to spend focused time developing their projects. Students will also be able to: Work alongside their peers. Exchange ideas. Continue experimenting with AI. Receive assistance when needed. Develop projects over time. Build relationships with other students interested in AI. This recurring structure is intended to encourage sustained experimentation rather than one-time participation. 3. Campus Showcases Campus Leads will also organize showcases where students can present what they have created using AI. These campus-wide events are expected to take place: Once each semester. The showcases provide students with an opportunity to demonstrate their work and celebrate what members of the campus community have been able to create. 4. Ongoing Community The Student Collective is also designed to provide an ongoing community where participating students can: Stay connected. Ask questions. Discover upcoming opportunities. Exchange knowledge. Support one another. Continue learning beyond individual events. Community participation will therefore continue throughout the program. What OpenAI Campus Leads Will Receive One of the major features of the OpenAI Student Collective is the package of resources provided to selected Campus Leads. ChatGPT Subscription Campus Leads will receive a ChatGPT subscription for the duration of the program . This should allow participants to gain direct experience with OpenAI s tools while helping students on their campuses understand how they can be used. Codex Credits Selected participants will also receive Codex credits for the duration of the program . Importantly, applicants are not required to have previous experience with Codex before applying. Funding for Campus Activities OpenAI will provide funding to support the organization of activities on participating campuses. This support is intended to help Campus Leads deliver workshops, Studio Hours, showcases, and other community-building activities. Additional Credits and Merchandise Campus Leads will receive additional credits and merchandise to support their campus activities and engagement. Training and Resources OpenAI will provide participants with training, resources, and guidance related to its latest tools and technology. This is particularly important because applicants are not expected to already be AI experts. Selected Campus Leads will receive support that helps them develop sufficient knowledge and confidence before introducing tools to other students. Access to the OpenAI Team Campus Leads will have access to the OpenAI team as part of their participation. This gives selected students an opportunity to learn within a community directly connected to the organization developing the technologies they will be introducing to their peers. Global Network of Campus Leads Participants will become part of a global network of OpenAI Campus Leads. This international community could provide opportunities to: Exchange ideas. Learn from activities taking place at other universities. Share successful approaches. Develop international connections. Discover how students from different academic and cultural contexts are using AI. Cash Stipend Every Semester Campus Leads will receive a cash stipend each semester in recognition of the time and leadership they contribute to the program. The information provided does not specify the exact monetary value of the stipend. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming a particular payment amount unless OpenAI provides further information during the selection or onboarding process. Potential OpenAI Headquarters Visit The program also includes opportunities for a headquarters visit in June 2027 , alongside other potential experiences during the program. The source information describes this as an opportunity rather than a guaranteed benefit for every Campus Lead. OpenAI Student Collective 2026–2027 Program Duration Campus Leads must be prepared to participate from: August 2026 through June 2027. Applicants must commit an average of: 4–6 hours per week. This is therefore a substantial academic-year leadership commitment rather than a short-term ambassador activity. Students should carefully consider their class schedules, extracurricular commitments, internships, employment, and other responsibilities before applying. Who Can Apply for the OpenAI Student Collective? OpenAI encourages undergraduate students from every discipline to apply. The program is not restricted to students studying: Computer science. Artificial intelligence. Software engineering. Data science. Mathematics. Information technology. Students studying humanities, social sciences, business, education, law, arts, sciences, healthcare-related subjects, and other fields can also apply if they satisfy the eligibility requirements. OpenAI states that it is looking for undergraduate students who are: Curious. Community-minded. Excited about AI. Interested in introducing other students to AI. Enthusiastic about OpenAI tools. Able to bring people together. OpenAI Student Collective Eligibility Requirements Applicants should carefully review the following requirements before submitting an application. 1. Applicants Must Be at Least 18 Years Old Campus Leads must be: 18 years of age or older. Applicants below 18 are therefore not eligible for the Campus Lead role based on the published requirements. 2. Applicants Must Be Undergraduate Students Applicants must be enrolled in an: Undergraduate college or university program as of August 2026. The application form explicitly states that the Campus Lead role is available only to undergraduate students. Applicants Must Graduate After December 2027 Eligible applicants must expect to complete their university or college studies: After December 2027. Applicants Must Commit 4–6 Hours Per Week Selected Campus Leads must be prepared to dedicate approximately: 4–6 hours each week from August 2026 through June 2027. OpenAI indicates that it is more interested in whether applicants are: Curious. Willing to learn. Able to bring people together. Interested in supporting other students. OpenAI will provide training and support to help selected students become more confident with its tools before they introduce those technologies on campus. Being relatively new to AI can even provide useful perspective because Campus Leads who remember the challenges of being beginners may be better positioned to create welcoming learning environments for students encountering AI tools for the first time. Major, course, field, or academic program. Applicants will also need to confirm whether they can dedicate 4–6 hours per week from August 2026 through June 2027. Candidates must submit a link to a video response lasting 60 seconds or less . The video must be accessible to anyone with the link because OpenAI states that it cannot review videos that require special access permissions. Awareness of how AI can benefit students. Video Question 2: Something You Made Happen on Campus Applicants must also respond to: What is something you helped make happen on campus? Again, the response must be provided through a video link lasting no more than 60 seconds. This question appears particularly relevant to the community-building nature of the Campus Lead role. Applicants are asked: What is the most important problem facing young people? How would you try to make progress on it? The response is limited to: 500 characters. Because the character limit is short, applicants should focus on identifying one clear problem and explaining a realistic approach rather than attempting to address many unrelated challenges. What Have You Changed Your Mind About Recently? Candidates must answer: What s something you ve changed your mind about recently? This response is also limited to: 500 characters. The question provides an opportunity to demonstrate reflection, intellectual openness, and an ability to reconsider previous assumptions. Applying With Another Student Campus Leads work in pairs. Application Deadline Applications for the OpenAI Student Collective Campus Lead opportunity close on: August 10, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time (PT). Applicants should also leave enough time to prepare and upload accessible links for the two required video responses. How to Prepare a Strong OpenAI Student Collective Application Although OpenAI does not provide a formula guaranteeing selection, candidates can use the application requirements to prepare strategically. 1. Demonstrate Community Leadership This is not simply an AI-user program. Campus Leads are expected to build communities. Applicants should therefore highlight experiences demonstrating their ability to: Organize students. Coordinate events. Lead initiatives. Build communities. Communicate across disciplines. Encourage participation. 2. Explain AI in an Accessible Way Campus Leads will introduce students from different academic backgrounds to AI. Avoid presenting yourself only as a highly technical user. Demonstrating an ability to make technology approachable to beginners may be equally valuable. 3. Prepare Strong 60-Second Videos Sixty seconds passes quickly. Before recording, identify: Your main message. One strong example. The impact. Why it matters. Avoid trying to include your entire résumé in the video. 4. Show Evidence of Initiative For the question about something you helped make happen on campus, choose an example where your contribution is clear. Explain what you actually did , rather than describing only what an organization or team accomplished collectively. 5. Keep Written Answers Focused With only 500 characters for some questions, every sentence matters. Start with the central idea and then briefly explain your reasoning or proposed action. 6. Check Video Permissions OpenAI specifically warns that it cannot review videos requiring access. Before submitting, test each video link in a private or incognito browser to ensure that someone without your account credentials can view it. 7. Confirm Your Availability The program requires 4–6 hours every week for approximately an academic year. Applicants should make sure they can realistically manage this commitment.
