title: Terre des Hommes Netherlands Opens Consultancy Opportunities in Ethiopia and Nigeria for Child Protection Research: Apply to Lead High-Impact Scoping Studies on Sexual Exploitation of Children
summary: Protecting children from exploitation remains one of the world s most urgent development priorities. As technology advances, migration patterns evolve, and cross-border movement increases, children continue to face growing risks of trafficking, online exploitation, sexual abuse, and other forms of violence. To better understand these challenges and strengthen child protection systems, Terre des Hommes Netherlands (TdH NL) has announced two major consultancy opportunities aimed at conducting comprehensive scoping studies in Ethiopia and Nigeria . These consultancies present an exceptional opportunity for experienced researchers, consultants, and research organizations specializing in child rights, human trafficking, qualitative research, and child protection systems to contribute directly to evidence-based programming that will shape future interventions across Africa. The two assignments form part of TdH Netherlands broader commitment to preventing all forms of Sexual Exploitation of Children (SEC) through systemic change rather than temporary interventions. Although each consultancy focuses on different geographical and thematic contexts, both share a common objective: generating reliable evidence that will guide future child protection programming and strengthen national and regional responses to child exploitation. About Terre des Hommes Netherlands Terre des Hommes Netherlands (TdH NL) is an international child rights organization dedicated to ensuring that every child grows up in an environment free from exploitation, abuse, and violence. Rather than focusing solely on responding to abuse after it occurs, the organization emphasizes long-term systemic change by addressing the underlying causes that expose children to exploitation. Its work is guided by five core principles: Children at the centre Safety and well-being Intersectionality Power awareness Sustainability TdH NL collaborates closely with governments, communities, children, civil society organizations, institutional partners, and the private sector to design evidence-based interventions that create lasting impact. Through these newly announced consultancies, the organization seeks to strengthen child protection systems by generating high-quality research that will inform future programming across East and West Africa. Why These Consultancy Opportunities Matter Across Africa, children continue to face increasing risks resulting from migration, poverty, conflict, climate change, technological advancement, and weak child protection systems. While governments and development partners have made significant investments in child protection, major knowledge gaps still exist regarding: Patterns of child migration Human trafficking networks Online child sexual exploitation Cross-border child protection Mental health vulnerabilities Digital safety Institutional response mechanisms Access to trauma-informed services Effectiveness of existing child protection systems Without reliable evidence, it becomes difficult for governments, NGOs, and development organizations to design interventions that address the actual needs of vulnerable children. The consultancy assignments therefore seek to bridge these knowledge gaps through extensive field research, stakeholder consultations, institutional mapping, and evidence generation that will guide future programming. Two Countries, Two Strategic Child Protection Initiatives Although announced separately, the Ethiopia and Nigeria consultancies complement one another by focusing on different dimensions of child exploitation. 1. Ethiopia: EmProtect+ Regional Child Protection Initiative The Ethiopia consultancy supports EmProtect+ , a regional initiative designed to protect children along high-risk transport corridors in East Africa. Unlike traditional child protection projects that focus only on local interventions, EmProtect+ adopts a regional systems-change approach. Its goal is to connect: National child protection systems Regional transport governance Cross-border cooperation Advocacy initiatives Knowledge-sharing platforms Evidence generation Institutional reforms The programme focuses particularly on children living and moving along the Addis Ababa–Moyale–Nairobi transport corridor, where migration exposes many children to trafficking and sexual exploitation. The Ethiopia study will determine whether the EmProtect+ model can successfully expand into the country. Understanding the Addis Ababa–Nairobi Transport Corridor The transport corridor connecting Addis Ababa and Nairobi has historically served as an important route for both trade and migration. Recent improvements in transportation infrastructure and the introduction of direct public transport between the two capitals have significantly increased cross-border movement. While this creates economic opportunities, it also introduces new child protection challenges. Research already indicates that many children from southern and central Ethiopia migrate through this corridor seeking: Employment Better educational opportunities Economic survival Escape from conflict Escape from forced marriage Escape from poverty Unfortunately, many become vulnerable to: Human trafficking Sexual exploitation Forced labour Abuse during transit Online exploitation Smuggling networks These growing risks make the corridor an important focus for future child protection interventions. Existing Child Protection Challenges in Ethiopia TdH NL s preliminary desk review identified several factors increasing children s vulnerability. These include: Poverty Many families continue to face severe economic hardship, encouraging children to migrate in search of employment. Climate Change Climate-induced displacement is becoming increasingly common across Ethiopia, forcing many households to relocate. Conflict Conflicts such as the Tigray War have displaced thousands of families and increased child migration. Rural-to-Urban Migration Children often leave rural communities hoping for better educational and employment opportunities. Early Marriage Some girls migrate to escape forced or early marriages. Online Exploitation Digital connectivity has created additional risks. Research cited by TdH NL indicates that approximately 10% of internet-using Ethiopian children aged 12–17 experienced online sexual exploitation in 2021. Weak Support Services Although Ethiopia has established mechanisms such as: One Stop Centres Child helplines National anti-trafficking coordination structures significant challenges remain, including: Limited trauma-informed care Shortage of trained psychosocial professionals Overcrowded services Limited cross-border coordination These findings underscore the need for stronger evidence and improved institutional coordination before expanding the EmProtect+ programme. Nigeria: SCROL 2.0 – Safe Minds Online Initiative The second consultancy focuses on Nigeria under TdH Netherlands SCROL 2.0 (Safe Minds Online) programme. Unlike the Ethiopia assignment, which centres on migration and transport corridors, the Nigeria consultancy addresses Online Child Sexual Exploitation (OCSE) . SCROL 2.0 builds upon lessons learned from the first phase of the programme and introduces a stronger emphasis on the relationship between: Mental health Digital safety Healthy online relationships Trauma-informed programming Child protection systems The programme recognizes that online exploitation cannot be addressed through law enforcement alone. Instead, it requires coordinated action involving: Families Schools Governments Civil society Technology companies Mental health professionals Child protection agencies Nigeria has been identified as a priority country for a future SCROL 2.0 pilot because of both its digital growth and the increasing number of online child exploitation cases reported nationally. Why Nigeria Was Selected Nigeria has become one of Africa s leading digital economies. Rapid internet adoption, smartphone use, fintech innovation, and technology entrepreneurship have created significant opportunities for economic growth. However, increased digital connectivity has also exposed children to new online risks. According to the Terms of Reference, Nigeria records the highest number of reports to the National Center for Missing Exploited Children (NCMEC) CyberTipline in West Africa. Between 2021 and 2022, reported cases increased by more than 100%, highlighting the urgent need for stronger preventive and protective measures. The country has already enacted legislation addressing Online Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (OCSEA), creating an enabling environment for evidence-based interventions, advocacy, and institutional strengthening. The consultancy will therefore generate the evidence needed to guide the implementation of a future SCROL 2.0 pilot programme across Nigeria. Comprehensive Research That Will Shape Future Child Protection Programmes Both consultancy assignments go far beyond conventional research projects. Rather than simply collecting data, the consultants will generate practical evidence that will directly influence the future design, implementation, and expansion of Terre des Hommes Netherlands child protection programmes in Ethiopia and Nigeria. The selected consultants will work closely with TdH NL to conduct rigorous qualitative research, engage with children and communities in ethical ways, map stakeholders, identify service gaps, and recommend strategic interventions that can produce long-term systemic change. The studies will also help TdH NL determine whether its flagship programmes—EmProtect+ in Ethiopia and SCROL 2.0 in Nigeria—can be successfully expanded into these countries. Ethiopia Consultancy: Research Objectives The Ethiopia consultancy is centred on understanding the prevalence of Sexual Exploitation of Children (SEC) and cross-border child trafficking along the Addis Ababa–Moyale–Nairobi transport corridor. The consultant will assess whether Ethiopia is ready for the expansion of the EmProtect+ programme by examining child protection systems, institutional capacity, and regional cooperation mechanisms. The study seeks to answer several important questions: 1. Understand the Risks Facing Children Along the Transport Corridor The consultant will investigate the different forms of sexual exploitation experienced by children living along or migrating through the Addis Ababa–Nairobi transport corridor. This includes examining: Offline sexual exploitation Online sexual exploitation Cross-border trafficking Domestic trafficking Exploitation occurring during migration Risks associated with transport hubs The research should provide a detailed understanding of where these risks occur and how they affect children. 2. Identify the Root Causes of Child Exploitation The consultant will analyse why children become vulnerable to exploitation. Key drivers include: Poverty Climate-induced migration Gender inequality Economic hardship Family instability Harmful social norms Lack of educational opportunities Primary data should be collected directly from: Children Caregivers Community members All research activities must comply with TdH NL s child safeguarding, accountability, and ethical participation standards. 3. Map National and Regional Stakeholders An important component of the study involves identifying institutions already working on child protection. The stakeholder mapping exercise should include: Government ministries Regional institutions Law enforcement agencies Civil society organizations International organizations Community-based organizations Private transport sector actors Regional cooperation mechanisms This mapping will help TdH NL establish partnerships for future implementation. 4. Evaluate Existing Child Protection Systems The consultant will assess: Existing child protection mechanisms Cross-border referral systems Trauma-informed services Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) services Psychosocial support services Educational opportunities Economic resilience programmes Vocational training opportunities The study should identify both strengths and gaps within these systems. 5. Recommend Future Programme Expansion Finally, the consultant will recommend: Geographic hotspots Strategic entry points Priority intervention areas Partnership opportunities Operational approaches These recommendations will guide the possible rollout of EmProtect+ in Ethiopia. Nigeria Consultancy: Research Objectives The Nigeria consultancy focuses on Online Child Sexual Exploitation (OCSE) and digital child protection under the SCROL 2.0 programme. Rather than concentrating on migration, this study examines how children experience exploitation within digital environments and how institutions can better prevent and respond to online abuse. The consultant will undertake the following research objectives. 1. Understand Online Risks Facing Children The consultant will identify: Types of online exploitation Digital platforms where abuse occurs Online behaviours increasing vulnerability Digital environments exposing children to harm The study should explore both emerging and existing online risks. 2. Examine Drivers of Online Exploitation Special attention will be given to factors such as: Mental health Parenting and caregiving environments Family support systems Emotional wellbeing Digital literacy Social vulnerabilities These factors will help explain why some children become more vulnerable to online exploitation than others. 3. Analyse Nigeria s Policy Landscape The consultancy will review: Existing child protection legislation OCSEA laws Reporting mechanisms Institutional response systems Digital safety policies The consultant should identify barriers preventing children from accessing support services and recommend improvements. 4. Map Key Stakeholders Stakeholder mapping will include: Government ministries Child protection agencies Civil society organizations Law enforcement agencies Telecommunications companies Technology companies Existing TdH NL partners The goal is to identify organizations capable of supporting future SCROL 2.0 implementation. 5. Evaluate Potential Partner Organizations Unlike many research assignments, this consultancy requires consultants to assess not only the existence of organizations but also their capacity to become implementation partners. Assessment criteria include: Experience Technical expertise Geographic reach Previous child protection work Organizational capacity Systems-strengthening experience 6. Assess TdH NL s Operational Model The consultant will determine how TdH NL s partner-led implementation model can be effectively introduced in Nigeria. This includes identifying: Opportunities Risks Partnership strategies Long-term sustainability measures The recommendations will guide future SCROL 2.0 programming. Expected Deliverables Both consultancies require consultants to produce comprehensive reports supported by high-quality evidence and practical recommendations. Although each assignment focuses on different thematic areas, the required outputs are remarkably similar. The final deliverables include: Comprehensive Context Analysis Consultants will prepare detailed reports examining: Social context Legal environment Institutional landscape Child protection ecosystem Existing programmes Current challenges Stakeholder Mapping Each consultancy requires a complete mapping of: Government institutions NGOs Community organizations Development partners Private sector actors Regional bodies The mapping should include recommendations on potential partnerships. Project Timelines Ethiopia Assignment The Ethiopia consultancy is expected to be completed by the end of 2026 . The work will be carried out in three phases: Phase 1 (September–October 2026) Preparatory activities including: Desk research Literature review Stakeholder mapping Development of interview guides Concept note preparation Phase 2 (November 2026) Fieldwork involving: Stakeholder interviews Community consultations Engagement with government institutions Transport sector consultations Phase 3 (December 2026) Final activities include: Data analysis Validation meetings Final report preparation Nigeria Assignment The Nigeria consultancy will take place during Q3 and Q4 of 2026 , with final deliverables expected in early November . The assignment includes: Phase 1 Desk review Stakeholder mapping Interview planning Concept note Phase 2 Eight to ten qualitative stakeholder interviews Six to eight focus group discussions with children and caregivers Phase 3 Data analysis Report writing Submission of final report Additionally, TdH NL plans to send a two-person mission to Nigeria during the research period to meet key stakeholders alongside the consultant and gain first-hand insight into the country s child protection landscape. Consultancy Budgets Both assignments offer competitive consultancy budgets. Ethiopia The consultancy budget is up to €20,000 , covering a maximum of 20 working days , including data collection costs and applicable taxes. Nigeria The consultancy budget ranges between €15,000 and €18,000 , inclusive of VAT, research costs, and travel expenses (excluding the travel costs of TdH NL s accompanying mission). Who Is Terre des Hommes Netherlands Looking For? Terre des Hommes Netherlands is seeking highly experienced consultants or consultancy firms capable of leading technically sound, ethical, and participatory research assignments. Given the sensitive nature of child protection and sexual exploitation, successful applicants must demonstrate not only strong research skills but also a deep commitment to safeguarding children and conducting responsible fieldwork. Both consultancies require professionals who can engage effectively with government institutions, civil society organizations, local communities, and children while producing high-quality evidence that can shape future programmes. Although the Ethiopia and Nigeria assignments focus on different contexts, the desired consultant profiles share many similarities. Fluency in relevant Ethiopian local languages. Proven experience conducting ethical, safe, and age-appropriate research involving children. TdH NL also notes that consultants or consultancy firms already based in Ethiopia will be strongly preferred because of their contextual understanding and ability to undertake fieldwork efficiently. Required Qualifications for the Nigeria Consultancy The Nigeria consultancy requires similar research expertise but with stronger emphasis on digital child protection and online safety. Preferred applicants should demonstrate: Extensive experience conducting qualitative and participatory research. Strong understanding of Online Child Sexual Exploitation (OCSE). Knowledge of child protection systems. Familiarity with mental health and psychosocial support systems. Ability to conduct ethical child-focused qualitative research. Fluency in English. Fluency in relevant Nigerian local languages. Strong contextual understanding of Nigeria. Preference will be given to consultants or agencies based in Nigeria to ensure cultural relevance and stronger stakeholder engagement. Unlike the Ethiopia assignment, the Nigeria Terms of Reference explicitly state that both individuals and consultancy agencies may apply , provided there are no conflicts of interest and all due diligence requirements are met. Commitment to Integrity and Child Safeguarding Because these consultancies involve children and vulnerable populations, TdH Netherlands places safeguarding and ethical conduct at the centre of the assignments. Successful consultants will be required to comply with the organization s Integrity Framework before signing a consultancy agreement. Among the mandatory requirements are the following: Signing the TdH NL Code of Conduct. Signing the Conflict of Interest Policy Declaration. Signing the Ethical Content Policy. For the Nigeria assignment, additional safeguarding responsibilities include: Safely recruiting and supervising researchers, translators, and enumerators. Ensuring all staff comply with safeguarding standards throughout the study. Preparing a safeguarding risk assessment based on Do No Harm principles. Developing clear referral pathways to child protection organizations and mental health service providers in case children disclose abuse. Obtaining TdH NL approval for all child assent and parental consent forms before fieldwork begins. These measures reinforce TdH NL s commitment to protecting children throughout the research process and ensuring that no harm results from participation in the studies. Application Requirements Applicants should carefully prepare a complete application package. While the submission email differs for each consultancy, the required documentation is largely the same. Applicants are expected to submit: A current Curriculum Vitae (CV) for individuals or organizational credentials for consultancy agencies. A motivation letter explaining their suitability for the assignment. A proposed approach and work plan outlining: Research methodology. Data collection strategy. Proposed timeline aligned with TdH NL s schedule. A detailed financial proposal showing: Daily consultancy rates. Travel expenses. Data collection costs. Applicable taxes. Overall budget breakdown. These documents will enable TdH NL to evaluate applicants technical competence, methodological approach, and financial feasibility. How to Apply Ethiopia Consultancy Interested applicants should submit their applications via email to Ms. Zoe de Melo , Programme Manager for the Sexual Exploitation of Children Programme. title: ERC Starting Grant 2027: A Complete Guide to Europe’s Prestigious Research Grant for Early-Career Scientists
summary: The European Research Council (ERC) has officially opened applications for the ERC Starting Grant 2027 (ERC-2027-STG) , one of the world s most prestigious research funding opportunities for outstanding early-career researchers. The grant is designed to empower talented scientists and scholars who have demonstrated exceptional promise during their early academic careers and are ready to establish themselves as independent research leaders. The ERC Starting Grant provides substantial financial support to ambitious researchers seeking to pursue groundbreaking scientific discoveries across any discipline. Through this funding scheme, researchers receive the freedom to develop innovative ideas, assemble international research teams, and conduct frontier research that has the potential to transform knowledge and society. Whether your expertise lies in engineering, medicine, natural sciences, social sciences, humanities, computer science, environmental studies, or any other field of research, the ERC Starting Grant offers a unique opportunity to secure world-class funding based solely on scientific excellence. About the European Research Council (ERC) The European Research Council (ERC), established by the European Commission, funds investigator-driven frontier research under the Horizon Europe Framework Programme. Unlike many traditional funding schemes that prioritize predefined thematic areas, ERC grants operate on a bottom-up approach , allowing applicants to propose research in any scientific field . The ERC s mission is to support excellent researchers whose innovative ideas have the potential to advance scientific knowledge significantly while strengthening Europe s global leadership in research and innovation. What is the ERC Starting Grant? The ERC Starting Grant is specifically designed for researchers who are transitioning from working under supervision to becoming independent Principal Investigators (PIs). It supports researchers who have already demonstrated excellent scientific achievements during the early stages of their careers and who possess the vision and capability to lead their own research programmes. Successful applicants receive funding to establish or strengthen their own research teams while pursuing ambitious, high-risk, and high-gain research projects. The programme emphasizes originality, scientific excellence, and the ability of the Principal Investigator to independently manage research activities and funding. Who Can Apply? Researchers from any nationality are eligible to apply for the ERC Starting Grant provided they meet the eligibility requirements. Applicants must have: Between 0 and 10 years of experience since successfully completing their PhD. A scientific track record demonstrating significant promise. Evidence of producing excellent supervised research. The ability to conduct independent research. Strong potential to become future research leaders. An outstanding and scientifically excellent research proposal. The ERC also provides guidance regarding eligibility extensions and the calculation of the PhD defence date under specific circumstances. Eligible Research Fields One of the greatest strengths of the ERC Starting Grant is its flexibility. Applicants may submit proposals in: Physical Sciences Engineering Mathematics Computer Science Life Sciences Medicine Agriculture Environmental Sciences Social Sciences Economics Political Science Psychology Education Humanities Arts Interdisciplinary Research Any other scientific discipline There are no predetermined research priorities , allowing applicants complete freedom to propose frontier research based on scientific excellence. Research Location Requirements Although researchers may come from anywhere in the world, the funded research must be carried out within an eligible host institution located in: An EU Member State, or A Horizon Europe Associated Country. The host institution can be: A university A research institute A public research organization A private research organization Any legally established research-performing institution eligible under Horizon Europe rules. Applicants may either remain at their current institution or relocate to another eligible institution. Host Institution Requirements Applications must be submitted by a single Principal Investigator (PI) on behalf of a host institution. The host institution is expected to: Provide an environment that supports excellent research. Guarantee the independence of the Principal Investigator. Allow the PI to lead the project autonomously. Enable independent management of the awarded funding. Applicants do not need to be formally employed by the host institution at the time of application. However, if awarded funding, both parties must have a mutual agreement regarding hosting the project. Building Your Research Team The ERC Starting Grant allows Principal Investigators to recruit research teams according to the needs of their proposed project. Research teams may include: Postdoctoral researchers PhD students Technicians Research assistants Specialists Collaborators Importantly: Team members may be of any nationality . Some team members may even be based outside Europe if necessary for the research. This flexibility enables researchers to build highly competitive international research collaborations. Funding Available The ERC Starting Grant offers significant financial support. Successful applicants may receive: Up to €1.5 million for a project lasting up to five years . Additional funding may also be requested when properly justified. Researchers may receive: Up to €1 million in additional funding to cover eligible research costs. Up to €2 million in additional funding for Principal Investigators relocating from non-associated third countries to an EU Member State or Associated Country. The ERC grant may fund: Up to 100% of eligible direct research costs . An additional 25% contribution toward indirect costs . This generous funding enables researchers to purchase equipment, recruit staff, conduct fieldwork, access research infrastructure, and implement ambitious scientific projects. How to Apply Applications can only be submitted through official ERC Calls for Proposals. Applicants should prepare a complete application package that includes: Administrative forms. The full scientific research proposal. Required supplementary documentation. Applications must be submitted before the official deadline through the appropriate submission system. Calls are published through: The ERC website. The EU Funding Tenders Portal. The Official Journal of the European Union. APPLY HERE Ethics Review Process Every proposal selected for funding undergoes an ethics review. This review ensures compliance with: Horizon Europe ethical principles. European Union legislation. National laws. International ethical standards. The Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. The European Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms. Applicants are required to complete: Ethics Issues Table (EIT) Ethics Self-Assessment (ESA) Providing a comprehensive Ethics Self-Assessment is essential because it helps reviewers understand how ethical issues will be managed throughout the project. The ethics review consists of three stages designed to ensure that funded research adheres to the highest ethical standards. Evaluation Process ERC proposals are evaluated exclusively on the basis of scientific excellence . International peer reviewers assess both: The quality and originality of the proposed research. The excellence and leadership potential of the Principal Investigator. No other evaluation criteria are used. This emphasis on excellence has made ERC grants among the most competitive and respected research funding schemes worldwide. ERC Research Data Platforms Researchers interested in previous ERC-funded projects can explore extensive research data through two major platforms. 1. ERC Dashboard The ERC Dashboard enables users to: Filter projects by country, year, panel, funding scheme, and other criteria. Export graphs and datasets. Analyze funding statistics. 2. ERC Research Information System (ERIS) ERIS provides advanced analytical tools including: Rich filtering options. Text mining capabilities. Interactive visualizations. Bibliometric information. Project outputs. Exportable datasets. These platforms help applicants understand funding trends and previous successful projects. Learning Resources for Applicants To assist applicants throughout the process, the ERC provides a comprehensive series of instructional videos covering: How to get started with an ERC grant. Writing a competitive scientific proposal. Preparing the administrative application. Understanding the evaluation process. Preparing for the ERC interview. Understanding ethics requirements. These learning materials provide practical guidance from ERC scientific officers and experienced experts. Key Documents Available Applicants are encouraged to carefully review the following official documents before preparing their proposal: ERC Work Programme 2027 Information for Applicants 2027 ERC Rules of Submission and Evaluation under Horizon Europe Guide for Peer Reviewers Gender Equality Plans Guidance Bias Awareness Guidance These documents explain the funding rules, evaluation criteria, eligibility conditions, and proposal preparation requirements in detail. Contact and Support Applicants seeking guidance can contact: Their National Contact Point (NCP). The European Research Council Executive Agency (ERCEA). These support services provide assistance regarding eligibility, proposal preparation, submission procedures, and administrative requirements. Important Dates Call Opens: 22 July 2026 Application Deadline: 14 October 2026 Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparing their proposals well in advance of the submission deadline to allow sufficient time for refining their research ideas, securing host institution commitments, completing ethics documentation, and gathering all required supporting materials. Why Consider Applying? The ERC Starting Grant is recognized globally as one of the most prestigious funding schemes for early-career researchers. Beyond the financial support, receiving an ERC grant significantly enhances a researcher s international reputation and opens doors to future collaborations, institutional leadership opportunities, and long-term research success. The programme is particularly attractive because it: Supports curiosity-driven frontier research. Funds projects in all scientific disciplines. Rewards scientific excellence above all else. Allows researchers considerable intellectual freedom. Encourages international collaboration. Provides generous funding for ambitious research programmes. Enables researchers to establish independent careers. Visit HERE for more information about the ERC Starting Grant 2027. Conclusion The ERC Starting Grant 2027 represents an exceptional opportunity for talented early-career researchers seeking to establish themselves as independent scientific leaders. With funding of up to €1.5 million over five years—plus additional funding where justified—the programme empowers researchers to pursue pioneering ideas without restrictions on research topics. By evaluating proposals solely on scientific excellence and supporting applicants from all nationalities, the ERC continues to foster world-class research that drives innovation and expands the frontiers of knowledge. Prospective applicants should begin preparing early, carefully review the official guidance documents, and ensure that their proposals are submitted before the 14th of October 2026 deadline.
